recipe: When receiving a string from C, explicitly verify its encoding rather than assuming it is UTF-8, since C strings may use encodings other than UTF-8.
trigger_condition: You are consuming a string that originates from a C or C-like foreign interface.
evidence: If you are using a string from C, you should check its encoding explicitly, rather than just assuming that it is UTF-8 like you can do in Rust.

recipe: When reading environment variables via env::var_os(), handle the returned Option<OsString> and then attempt conversion to a Rust string, checking the resulting Result for errors indicating invalid Unicode data.
trigger_condition: You need to read an environment variable and use it as a Rust string.
evidence: If the environment variable exists you will get a Some(os_string), which you can then try to convert to a Rust string. This yields a Result, so that your code can detect errors in case the environment variable did not in fact contain valid Unicode data.

recipe: On Unix, use OsStrExt::from_bytes and OsStrExt::as_bytes for inexpensive byte-slice conversions with OsStr.
trigger_condition: You are on a Unix platform and need to convert between OsStr and byte slices.
evidence: On Unix, OsStr implements the std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt trait, which augments it with two methods, from_bytes and as_bytes. These do inexpensive conversions from and to byte slices.

recipe: On Windows, call OsStrExt::encode_wide to get an iterator of u16 values, then append a terminating nul character to produce a native Windows string.
trigger_condition: You are on Windows and need to convert an OsStr into a native Windows wide string.
evidence: On Windows, OsStr implements the std::os::windows::ffi::OsStrExt trait, which provides an encode_wide method. This provides an iterator that can be collected into a vector of u16. After a nul characters is appended, this is the same as a native Windows string.

recipe: On Windows, use OsStringExt::from_wide to convert a native Windows wide string (without its terminating nul) into an OsString.
trigger_condition: You are on Windows and have a native Windows wide string that you need to wrap in an OsString.
evidence: On Windows OsString implements the std::os::windows:ffi::OsStringExt trait, which provides a from_wide method to convert a native Windows string (without the terminating nul character) to an OsString.

recipe: For limited, inexpensive byte-level conversions with OsStr on any platform, use OsStr::as_encoded_bytes and OsStr::from_encoded_bytes_unchecked.
trigger_condition: You need a quick byte-level conversion with OsStr and do not require full platform-native string handling.
evidence: For limited, inexpensive conversions from and to bytes, see OsStr::as_encoded_bytes and OsStr::from_encoded_bytes_unchecked.

recipe: For basic string processing on an OsStr, use OsStr::slice_encoded_bytes to work with the underlying byte sequence.
trigger_condition: You need to perform basic string operations on an OsStr's underlying byte data.
evidence: For basic string processing, see OsStr::slice_encoded_bytes.
